q.s: Which irrigation method is recorded for Harappan agriculture, which also practised double cropping?
q.x: The notes record double cropping with wooden ploughs and flood irrigation; canal irrigation in Punjab and Sindh is not proved.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Canal irrigation is fully proved for Harappan Punjab and Sindh.
The Harappans did not use the plough.
Rice was the staple crop of Mohenjodaro.
q.x: Double cropping is recorded; canal irrigation is not proved, a ploughed field was found at Kalibangan, and wheat and barley were the staples.

q.s: The Late Harappan post-cremation burials known as Cemetery H were found at:
q.x: Cemetery H, with Late Harappan post-cremation burials, is at Harappa.

q.s: Which of the following burial evidence–site pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Women buried with jasper and agate beads – Rakhigarhi
q.x: Cemetery H is at Harappa.

q.s: According to H.D. Sankalia, rice was first harvested in Andhra Pradesh during the:
q.x: Sankalia placed the first rice harvest in Andhra in the Iron Age, represented by the Megalithic Black and Red Ware culture.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Megalithic (Iron Age) site of Andhra Pradesh mentioned in the notes?
q.x: Brahmagiri, Nagarjunakonda, Gudivada and Jonnawada are Megalithic sites; Kalibangan is a Harappan site in Rajasthan.

q.s: The Udgatri priest was associated with which Veda?
q.x: The Udgatri chanted the Samaveda; Hotri = Rigveda, Adhvaryu = Yajurveda, Brahman = Atharvaveda.

q.s: Which of the following Veda–priest pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The Samaveda priest was the Udgatri; the Hotri belonged to the Rigveda.

q.s: The Buddha delivered his first sermon, the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta, at:
q.x: The first sermon, on the Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path, was given at Sarnath to his five former companions.

q.s: Vesak (Buddha Purnima) commemorates all of the following events in the Buddha's life EXCEPT:
q.x: Vesak marks birth, enlightenment and death; the first sermon is not part of it.

q.s: Makkhali Gosala, a companion of Mahavira for about six years, founded the:
q.x: Makkhali Gosala founded the Ajivika sect.

q.s: Who survived Mahavira and became the first Thera (head of the Jain Sangha)?
q.x: Only Arya Sudharma survived Mahavira and became the first Thera; Bhadrabahu was the sixth Thera.

q.s: Ashoka began his Dhammayatras in his 11th regnal year with a visit to:
q.x: The Dhammayatras began with Bodh Gaya in his 11th regnal year.

q.s: At Lumbini, in his 21st regnal year, Ashoka reduced the land tax (bhaga) to:
q.x: The Rummindei pillar records the reduction of the tax at Lumbini to one-eighth.

q.s: Who explained the decline of the Mauryan Empire as the result of a Brahmanical reaction?
q.x: H.P. Shastri's theory rests on Ashoka's pro-Buddhist policy and ban on sacrifices; Romila Thapar blamed over-centralisation.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: H.P. Shastri blamed over-centralisation for the decline of the Mauryas.
Romila Thapar blamed over-centralisation for the decline of the Mauryas.
The Sungas, who succeeded the Mauryas, were Buddhists.
q.x: Thapar stressed over-centralisation; Shastri saw a Brahmanical reaction to Ashoka's ban on sacrifices, and the Sungas were Brahmins.

q.s: The monolithic Ashokan pillars were made of sandstone quarried at:
q.x: The pillars were of Chunar sandstone; they cluster in the Ganga plain because river transport made moving them easier.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Ashokan pillars is correct?
o: Their stone was quarried at each pillar site.
They were made of granite from the Deccan.
They cluster in the Ganga plain because river transport made moving them easier.
Most of them stand in South India.
q.x: The Chunar sandstone monoliths had to be moved, so they cluster along the Ganga.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an Ashokan edict site?
q.x: Besnagar is known for the Heliodorus pillar; Girnar, Kalsi and Dhauli have Ashokan rock edicts.

q.s: Kalhana's Rajatarangini links Kashmir with Ashoka and names his son as:
q.x: The Rajatarangini names Jalauka as Ashoka's son.

q.s: The Sanskrit play Mudrarakshasa, written by Vishakhadatta, deals with:
q.x: The Mudrarakshasa is about Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya; the Ramagupta-Dhruvadevi story is in his Devichandraguptam.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Mudrarakshasa deals with Ramagupta and Dhruvadevi.
The Devichandraguptam was written by Kalidasa.
The Mudrarakshasa is about Samudragupta's conquests.
The Devichandraguptam deals with Ramagupta, Dhruvadevi and Chandragupta II.
q.x: Both plays are Vishakhadatta's; the Mudrarakshasa is about Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya.

q.s: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-hien visited India during the reign of:
q.x: Fa-hien visited c. 399-412 CE, in the reign of Chandragupta II; he came before Xuan Zang and I-Qing.

q.s: Harishena, author of the Allahabad Pillar Inscription, was the court poet of:
q.x: Harishena was Samudragupta's court poet; the Udayagiri inscription is of Chandragupta II's minister Virasena.

q.s: Which of the following about Gupta guilds is NOT correct?
o: Some guilds maintained their own armed bodies.
The Dashpur inscription was composed by Vatsabhatti.
The head of a guild was called the Sarthavaha.
The Indore copper plate recording an oil-men's guild belongs to Skandagupta's reign.
q.x: The Sarthavaha was the caravan leader; the guild head was the Jyeshthaka.

q.s: The Indore copper plate inscription, which records an endowment with a guild of oil-men, belongs to the reign of:
q.x: It belongs to Skandagupta's reign.

q.s: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh, the earliest Panchayatana temple of North India, belongs to the:
q.x: The earliest surviving free-standing Hindu temples, including Deogarh (Lalitpur district, UP), are Gupta.

q.s: In which district of Uttar Pradesh is the Dashavatara temple of Deogarh located?
q.x: Deogarh is in Lalitpur district.

q.s: The Agamas are the sacred texts of:
q.x: The Agamas are Jain scriptures; the Tripitaka is Buddhist and the Brahmanas are Vedic ritual texts.

q.s: Which of the following tradition–text pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The Brahmanas are Vedic ritual texts, not Buddhist.

q.s: Who wrote the Ashtanga Hridaya?
q.x: Vagbhata wrote the Ashtanga Hridaya; Charaka (Kushana age) wrote the Charaka Samhita.

q.s: Which of the following scholar–work pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: Charaka wrote the Charaka Samhita; the Ashtanga Hridaya is Vagbhata's.

q.s: The Gupta princess Prabhavatigupta, who ruled as regent of the Vakataka kingdom, was the daughter of:
q.x: Prabhavatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, married Rudrasena II; her regency gave the Guptas indirect control of the Deccan.

q.s: The Prakrit work Setubandha was written by the Vakataka ruler:
q.x: Setubandha is by Pravarasena II, son of Prabhavatigupta.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms?
o: Land measurement covering the whole empire
Abolition of the privileges of khuts and muqaddams
Reclaiming milk, waqf and inam lands as khalisa
Assessment of land revenue on measurement
q.x: Measurement covered only a belt around the Doab and Delhi, not the whole empire.

q.s: Which Sultan of Delhi was the first to dig canals?
q.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the first Sultan to dig canals; Firuz Shah later built many more.

q.s: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq replaced Alauddin's measurement on khalisa land with:
q.x: He reverted to crop-sharing (batai).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Indian trabeate style of building?
q.x: The true arch with keystone came with Indo-Islamic architecture; the trabeate style used lintel, pillar and corbel.

q.s: Surkhi, used in Indo-Islamic buildings, was:
o: Brick dust used in lime mortar
q.x: Surkhi was brick dust mixed in lime mortar.

q.s: Under the Mughals, the Faujdar and Amalguzar were officials of the:
q.x: The Sarkar (district) had the Faujdar and Amalguzar; the Suba had the Subedar and Diwan.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a pargana-level official in the Mughal administration?
q.x: Shiqdar, amil, qanungo and chaudhari worked at the pargana; the Faujdar was a sarkar official.

q.s: Which of the following was a major cause of the weakening of the Mughal Empire after Aurangzeb?
o: Transfer of the capital to Agra
Long Deccan wars that drained the treasury
q.x: Aurangzeb's prolonged Deccan wars drained the treasury and weakened the empire.

q.s: The Nishat Bagh on the Dal Lake was laid out by:
q.x: Nishat Bagh was built by Asaf Khan, Nur Jahan's brother.

q.s: The Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar was laid out by:
q.x: Shalimar Bagh, Srinagar is Jahangir's; the Shalimar Gardens at Lahore are Shah Jahan's.

q.s: The Bhakti and Sufi saints enriched regional languages mainly because they:
o: Wrote only in Sanskrit and Persian
Preached in the language of the masses
Were patronised by the Mughal court
q.x: They preached in the people's language, which enriched Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Punjabi and others.

q.s: Nizamuddin Auliya's famous remark 'Hunuz Dilli dur ast' (Delhi is still far) was said of:
q.x: It was said of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq; Nizamuddin never visited the Sultans' court.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya is correct?
o: He regularly attended the Sultans' court.
He belonged to the Suhrawardi order.
He lived under only one Sultan.
He never visited the court of the Delhi Sultans.
q.x: Nizamuddin, a Chishti saint who saw seven Sultans, kept away from the court.

q.s: The Battle of Assaye (1803), where Arthur Wellesley defeated Scindia and the Bhonsle, was part of the:
q.x: Assaye and Laswari belong to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought in the Second Anglo-Maratha War?
q.x: Kirki (Khadki, 1817) belongs to the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

q.s: Until 1690, the headquarters of the Dutch on the Coromandel coast was:
q.x: Pulicat was the Dutch headquarters until 1690 (later Nagapattinam).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Dutch settlement on the Andhra coast?
q.x: Yanam was a French settlement.

q.s: Madras was founded in 1639 by:
q.x: Francis Day founded Madras; Aungier is the 'founding father' of Bombay.

q.s: Which of the following person–role pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: Aungier is the 'founding father' of Bombay.

q.s: The Danish-Halle Mission at Tranquebar (1706) was founded by:
q.x: Ziegenbalg founded the mission and translated the New Testament into Tamil.

q.s: The first translation of the Bible into Telugu was made by:
q.x: Benjamin Schulz made the first Telugu Bible translation (printed at Halle 1746-47).

q.s: The Doctrine of Lapse was withdrawn after the Revolt of 1857 by:
q.x: Canning withdrew it after 1857; Dalhousie had applied it.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Dalhousie withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse in 1856.
Awadh was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
By 1856 British India extended from the Hindukush to Burma.
The lapse annexations won the loyalty of the taluqdars.
q.x: Canning withdrew the Doctrine after 1857; Awadh was annexed for alleged misgovernance, and the annexations alienated rulers and taluqdars.

q.s: Who was the Governor of Bengal during the Bengal Famine of 1770?
q.x: John Cartier was governor in 1770; Warren Hastings came in 1772.

q.s: The Bengal Famine of 1770 is estimated to have killed about what share of Bengal's population?
q.x: About ten million people, roughly one-third of the population, died.

q.s: Nellore and Chittoor, which completed Company control over the Andhra region, were annexed in 1801 from the:
q.x: The 1801 takeover of the Carnatic Nawab's territories brought Nellore and Chittoor under the Company.

q.s: The Nizam of Hyderabad was defeated by the Marathas in 1795 at the Battle of:
q.x: After Kharda (1795) the Nizam blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality and turned to Raymond's French battalions.

q.s: The French battalions in the Nizam's service before the 1798 Subsidiary Alliance were commanded by:
q.x: Monsieur Raymond commanded the French corps of the Nizam.

q.s: Under the Permanent Settlement (1793), the ownership of land was recognised as vested in the:
q.x: The zamindars were made owners with hereditary, transferable rights, while many cultivators became tenants-at-will.

q.s: Under colonial rule, jute was grown mainly in:
q.x: Jute was chiefly a Bengal crop; tea was grown in Assam and opium in Bengal-Bihar and Malwa.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of colonial cash crop and main region is NOT correct?
q.x: Tea was grown mainly in Assam, not the Deccan.

q.s: Wood's Despatch (1854) was issued when the Governor-General of India was:
q.x: Sir Charles Wood issued it on 19 July 1854 under Lord Dalhousie.

q.s: Sir Charles Wood issued his Despatch of 1854 in his capacity as:
o: President of the Board of Control
Chairman of the Court of Directors
q.x: Wood was President of the Board of Control.

q.s: The 'Downward Filtration Theory' in Indian education is credited to:
q.x: The theory of educating a few upper and middle class people so that learning would filter down is credited to Macaulay.

q.s: The introduction of railways, the modern postal system and the telegraph in India is credited to:
q.x: All three are credited to Dalhousie.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT introduced by Lord Dalhousie?
q.x: The Vernacular Press Act (1878) was passed under Lytton.

q.s: Which commission classified the civil services into Imperial, Provincial and Subordinate?
q.x: The Aitchison Commission (1886) made the three-tier classification.

q.s: The Statutory Civil Service, reserving one-sixth of covenanted posts for Indians by nomination, was introduced by:
q.x: Lytton introduced the Statutory Civil Service (1879).

q.s: Under the dyarchy of the Government of India Act, 1919, finance in the provinces was a:
q.x: Finance stayed reserved with the Governor and Executive Council, a key reason dyarchy largely failed.

q.s: Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in the year:
q.x: The Brahmo Sabha was founded on 20 August 1828.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT founded by Raja Rammohan Roy?
q.x: The Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) was founded by Debendranath Tagore.

q.s: B.R. Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in:
q.x: The Sabha was founded in 1924.

q.s: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha led by Ambedkar took place in 1930 at:
q.x: The Kalaram temple is at Nashik; the 1927 tank satyagraha was at Mahad.

q.s: Which Justice Party leader from Andhra became Premier of Madras in 1937?
q.x: K.V. Reddy Naidu of Eluru, a minister in 1920, became Premier in 1937.

q.s: Which of the following about Justice Party leaders of Andhra is NOT correct?
o: M. Suryanarayana's 1922 separate-Andhra resolution was withdrawn at Panagal Raja's urging.
Bobbili Raja was a delegate to the Second Round Table Conference.
K.V. Reddy Naidu became Premier of Madras in 1937.
C.R. Reddy moved a no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja's ministry in 1923.
q.x: The resolution was withdrawn at A.P. Patro's urging.

q.s: The Depressed Classes Mission (1906) at Bombay was founded by:
q.x: V.R. Shinde founded it; M.C. Rajah headed the All India Depressed Classes Association (1926).

q.s: The first president of the All India Anti-Untouchability League (later Harijan Sevak Sangh) was:
q.x: G.D. Birla was its first president.

q.s: The political guru of Gopal Krishna Gokhale was:
q.x: Gokhale was a disciple of Ranade.

q.s: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the 1905 session of the Indian National Congress held at:
q.x: He presided at Banaras in 1905.

q.s: The Extremists popularised which of the following festivals to rouse national feeling?
q.x: Tilak used the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals; such Hindu symbolism kept most Muslims away from the Extremist movement.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Extremists is correct?
o: They were socially radical but politically moderate.
Most Indian Muslims joined their movement.
They were politically radical but socially conservative.
They avoided religious symbols in politics.
q.x: They used Hindu symbols such as the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals, which kept most Muslims away.

q.s: The Indian Home Rule Society was founded in London in 1905 by:
q.x: Shyamji Krishnavarma founded the Society and India House.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT founded by Shyamji Krishnavarma?
q.x: The Paris Indian Society was founded by Madame Cama with S.R. Rana.

q.s: Annie Besant bought the Madras Standard in 1914 and renamed it:
q.x: The Madras Standard became New India.

q.s: The Commonwealth of India Bill (1925) was introduced in the House of Commons by:
q.x: George Lansbury introduced the Bill, which sought Dominion Status.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report (1928)?
o: Joint electorates with reservation of seats for minorities
Residuary powers vested in the Centre
q.x: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates and recommended joint electorates with reserved seats.

q.s: The Khilafat Movement was triggered by the treaty that dismembered Turkey in 1920, the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Sevres (May 1920) triggered the movement.

q.s: The Caliphate was abolished by Mustafa Kemal Pasha in:
q.x: It was abolished in 1924, ending the relevance of the Khilafat agitation.

q.s: The first atom bomb was dropped on 6 August 1945 on:
q.x: Hiroshima on 6 August; Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Axis powers in the Second World War?
q.x: China fought on the Allied side.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a part of the Quit India Resolution of August 1942?
o: Acceptance of Dominion Status after the war
Immediate end of British rule in India
A provisional government after British withdrawal
A mass struggle under Gandhi's leadership
q.x: The resolution demanded an immediate end of British rule, not post-war Dominion Status.

q.s: The phrase 'Quit India' was coined by:
q.x: Yusuf Meherally coined it.

q.s: Gandhi's Quit India writings of 1942 appeared in the journal:
q.x: They appeared in Harijan.

q.s: The first Interim Government of India was formed on:
q.x: The Interim Government was formed on 2 September 1946.

q.s: The Mountbatten Plan for the partition of India was announced on:
q.x: The Plan was announced on 3 June 1947; Attlee's announcement was on 20 February 1947.

q.s: 'Naa Jeevita Yatra' is the autobiography of:
q.x: It is Prakasam's autobiography.

q.s: Konda Venkatappayya, who became AICC Secretary in 1923, was a lawyer from:
q.x: He was born at Guntur in 1866.

q.s: Gandhi drew the idea of the dignity of labour from:
o: Tolstoy's The Kingdom of God is Within You
q.x: Ruskin's Unto This Last taught dignity of labour; Thoreau taught breaking unjust laws.

q.s: Which of the following source–idea pairs, as taken by Gandhi, is NOT correct?
q.x: Thoreau taught the right to break unjust laws; dignity of labour came from Ruskin.

q.s: Who was sentenced in the Kakinada Bomb Case and wrote 'Andaman Jeevitam'?
q.x: Prativadi Bhayankarachari was sent to the Cellular Jail and wrote 'Andaman Jeevitam'.

q.s: The Kakinada Bomb Case followed a police attack on the satyagrahis of the:
q.x: Circle inspector Mustafa Ali attacked the Seethanagaram satyagrahis.

q.s: 'Feathers and Stones', a diary written in Ahmednagar Fort during the Quit India period, is by:
q.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote it.

q.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Andhra in 1942 is NOT correct?
q.x: Venkatarangayya was linked with the Andhra University resolution for Gandhi's release.

q.s: The States Department set up in July 1947 to integrate the princely states was headed by:
q.x: Patel headed it, with V.P. Menon as Secretary.

q.s: In the integration of princely states, the Kathiawar states were consolidated into:
q.x: The Kathiawar states formed the Union of Saurashtra.

q.s: The police firing during the Mulki agitation of 1952 in Hyderabad was inquired into by:
q.x: Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy inquired into the firing near City College.

q.s: The Mulki agitation of 1952 took place under the ministry of:
q.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao was Chief Minister of Hyderabad State.

q.s: A Bill under Article 3 for forming new States can be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the:
q.x: Article 3 Bills need the President's recommendation and are passed by simple majority.

q.s: Which of the following about Articles 2 to 4 is NOT correct?
o: Article 2 deals with admission of new States from outside India.
An Article 3 Bill needs the President's recommendation.
A law under Article 3 is deemed an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368.
The time limit for the State legislature's views was added by the 5th Amendment.
q.x: Article 4 says such laws are not Article 368 amendments.

q.s: Amaravati was chosen as the capital of Andhra Pradesh in the year:
q.x: Amaravati was chosen in 2015, with about 33,000 acres pooled for it.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the three capitals proposed under Andhra Pradesh's three-capitals plan?
q.x: The plan proposed Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Kurnool; the High Court ruled against it on 3 March 2022.

q.s: The Iron Age megaliths of Andhra are popularly called:
q.x: They are known as Rakshasa Gullu (Kurambara Gullu in Chittoor, Morivara Gullu in Anantapur).

q.s: In Chittoor district, the Iron Age megaliths are locally called:
q.x: They are Kurambara Gullu in Chittoor and Morivara Gullu in Anantapur.

q.s: The Sudarshana lake was originally built under Chandragupta Maurya by:
q.x: Pushyagupta built it; Tushaspha added canals under Ashoka.

q.s: The Sudarshana lake was repaired in 150 CE for Rudradaman I by the Pahlava minister:
q.x: Suvishakha repaired it; Chakrapalita repaired it again under Skandagupta.

q.s: Under the Satavahanas, bhaga, the king's share of the produce, was:
q.x: Bhaga was one-sixth of the produce.

q.s: The main centre of the Mahasanghika school of Buddhism in Andhra was:
q.x: Dhanyakataka (Amaravati) was the Mahasanghika centre.

q.s: The first Buddhist acharya in Andhra, who founded the Chaityakavada (worship of chaityas), was:
q.x: Mahadeva Bhikshu founded the Chaityakavada.

q.s: The title 'Trisamudradhipati' was assumed by the Vishnukundin ruler:
q.x: Madhava Varma II took the titles Trisamudradhipati and Vidyadvijaguru.

q.s: Which of the following Vishnukundin ruler–title pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: Vidyadvijaguru was a title of Madhava Varma II.

q.s: The Kakatiya rulers turned from Jainism to Shaivism from the time of:
q.x: The Shaiva turn came under Prola II and Rudradeva, after which Jain–Saiva conflicts grew.

q.s: The Kashmiri poet Bilhana wrote the Vikramankadevacharita about:
q.x: It celebrates the Kalyani Chalukya ruler Vikramaditya VI.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Vachana literature of the Virashaiva movement?
q.x: Nagavarma II wrote the Kavyavalokana; the vachanakaras include Basavanna, Allama and Akka.

q.s: Which of the following work–author pairs is NOT correct?
o: Andhra Mahabharatam (Adi and Sabha parvas) – Nannaya
q.x: The Uttara Harivamsa is by Nachana Somana.

q.s: Tikkana dedicated his Telugu Mahabharatam to:
q.x: Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita and dedicated his Bharatam to Hariharanatha.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, the head of a merchant guild was called:
q.x: The guild head was called Setti or Sreshthi.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of Kakatiya merchant guilds?
o: Guilds had their own seals and emblems
Trade was a royal monopoly of the king
q.x: The king held no monopoly over trade.

q.s: The title 'Andhra Bhoja' belonged to:
q.x: Andhra Bhoja was Krishnadevaraya's title.

q.s: Prolaya Vema Reddi, founder of the Reddi kingdom, built the Patala Ganga steps at:
q.x: The Mutnuri inscription records his Patala Ganga steps at Srisailam.

q.s: Which of the Deccan Sultanates was the last to break away from the Bahmanis and the last to fall?
q.x: Golconda broke away in 1518 and fell in 1687.

q.s: Which of the following Deccan Sultanate–capital pairs is NOT correct?
q.x: The Imad Shahis ruled Berar from Ellichpur; Bidar was the Barid Shahi capital.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya supported the Portuguese capture of Goa (1510) from Bijapur by:
q.x: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510.

q.s: The Ramappa temple is an example of which temple style?
q.x: Ramappa is a Kakatiya Vesara temple.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (temple – style)?
q.x: Lepakshi is in the Vijayanagara style.

q.s: The Virupaksha temple at Hampi is popularly called the:
q.x: Virupaksha, the first and largest temple of Hampi, is called the Pampapati temple.

q.s: Which of the following about the Virupaksha temple at Hampi is NOT correct?
o: It is popularly called the Pampapati temple.
It was enlarged by Lakkana Dandesha under Devaraya I.
Krishnadevaraya added its central hall and eastern gopuram in 1510.
Its Ranga mandapa ceiling shows Vidyaranya in a procession.
q.x: Lakkana Dandesha enlarged it under Devaraya II.

q.s: In the Madras Presidency, the Supreme Court of Madras was established in:
q.x: The Madras Supreme Court dates from 1801.

q.s: The Madras Native Association (1852) was founded by:
q.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty founded it.

q.s: The first president of the Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884) was:
q.x: P. Rangaiah Naidu was president and P. Anandacharlu secretary.

q.s: The accused in the Kakinada Riot Case (1907) were defended by:
q.x: Nyapati Subbarao defended them.

q.s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle was triggered by an attack on a tribal meeting in 1967 near:
